title: Checkpoint Cascade Launch Grid and Signal Cabinet
content:
Overview:
This sheet defines a lightweight, repeatable 'checkpoint cascade' for feature launches that combines a roadmapped traffic ramp, discrete gating checks, and an actionable signal cabinet (what to look at + who acts). The goal is to replace long freeform launch notes with a compact operational checklist and scorecard that Product Ops, Eng SRE, and Product Owners can run during canary -> ramp -> general availability (GA).

How to use this sheet:
- Fill owner and status columns before starting a gate.
- Run smoke suite and ingestion checks at each checkpoint (see Quick Tests).
- Evaluate KPIs; compute Decision Score (formula below). If Decision Score < threshold, hold and investigate — use rollback/mitigation playbook.

High-level traffic ramp (recommended default):
- Canary 1 (internal): 0.5% traffic, 1 hour steady -> checkpoint A
- Canary 2 (external small cohort): 2% traffic, 6 hours steady -> checkpoint B
- Gradual ramp: 10% -> 25% -> 50% over 24–72 hours with checkpoints at each step (C, D, E)
- GA: 100% after final gate F sign-off

Checkpoint matrix (columns to track in the sheet):
- Gate ID: A, B, C, D, E, F
- Target traffic %
- Owner: product-owner / eng-sre / product-ops
- Quick smoke pass? (yes/no)
- Key KPI snapshots (see below)
- Decision Score (numeric)
- Outcome (proceed/hold/rollback)
- Notes / triggers observed

Key KPIs and thresholds (these are configurable per-feature):
- Latency p95 (app-layer): ideal < 220ms, guarded threshold < 400ms
- Error rate (5xx + client-specified failures): ideal < 0.2%, guarded threshold < 1.0%
- Token cost per 1M output tokens (hosted): expected baseline ±20%
- Throughput: tail throughput within 15% of expected for target concurrency
- Quality/regression signals (synthetic eval): top-1 accuracy on canonical prompt set - no negative delta > 3%
- Consumer-facing rate-limited or degraded endpoints: zero critical regressions

Decision Score (quick composite):
- Score = (LatencyScore + ErrorScore + CostScore + QualityScore + ThroughputScore) / 5
- Each subscore is 0..100 where 100 = best. Map KPI to subscores using linear mapping between ideal and guarded thresholds.
- Rule of thumb: proceed if Score >= 80; hold for 60–79; rollback if < 60 or if any single KPI crosses a hard abort condition (see Abort Conditions).

Abort Conditions (immediate rollback or stop and investigate):
- Sustained error rate > 3% for 5+ minutes OR spikes above 5% even for 1 minute
- Latency p95 > 800ms for 10 minutes at target traffic
- Quality regression where canonical prompt failure mode causes user-visible incorrectness for > 5% of sampled requests
- Billing anomaly: cost per 1M tokens > 3x baseline without mitigation explanation

Signal Cabinet (what to inspect at each gate):
- Platform metrics: request/sec, p50/p95/p99 latency, error breakdown by type and route
- Observability: traces for slow requests, SLI drift charts, top slow handlers
- Cost telemetry: estimated hourly spend delta vs baseline by model/route
- User-facing errors: Sentry/err-trace spike lists and sample payloads
- Quality evals: 50-sample synthetic prompt set, human review notes if any
- Feature-specific metrics: adoption funnel, retention signals (if applicable)

Quick Tests (smoke checklist to run at every gate):
1) Can make successful end-to-end request from known-good client (3 requests, success 100%)
2) KV-cache warming sanity, top-3 hot prefixes hit in 30s
3) Billing estimator sanity: projected hourly spend within expected bounds
4) No new 5xx error classes in top-10 errors
5) Sample generation matches guardrail regexes (structured output checks)

Operational playbooks (short form):
- Hold: Pause ramping for current gate. Notify owners + oncall. Run triage (run smoke tests, gather traces, escalate to model infra). Document root cause hypothesis in ticket (link in sheet).
- Mitigate: Throttle traffic, enable conservative quantization/backup model variant, or routing to dedicated pool (if configured).
- Rollback: Flip routing to previous stable model version and reduce traffic to internal-only. Open incident and follow SRE incident runbook.

Owners & escalation contacts (fill before GTM):
- Product Ops lead: Aisha Raman (primary)
- Product Owner: Marcus Chen
- Eng SRE oncall: rotate-sre@redwood.ai (use runbook for escalation)
- Model Infra lead (for quantization/fallbacks): Lena Ortiz
- Legal / Compliance contact (if gating on private deployments): Tomáš Novák

Post-launch quick retro signals (24–72h):
- Customer support tickets tagged with feature-x: target < 0.1% of usage events
- Stabilized Decision Score trend: average >= 85 across final three gates
- Cost delta normalized: within committed run budget or flagged for cost ops review

Common gotchas and notes from past launches:
- Don’t rely on a single synthetic eval — always cross-check with small human sample for hallucination patterns
- Warm caches before promoting to larger cohorts; cold-cache performance is a frequent surprise
- Predefine the backup routing policy (variant, quantization profile) so it’s a one-click mitigation

Appendix: quick mapping for owner responsibilities:
- Product Ops: orchestrate the checkpoint run, own the checklist and communication cadence
- Product Owner: set KPI targets and approve progression decisions with eng-sre
- Eng SRE: validate platform telemetry, run rollbacks and throttle policies
- Model Infra: provide fallback model variants and cost/quant profiles

Notes / open questions (to capture in ticket before final sign-off):
- Do we need a dedicated cost guardrail for model embeddings separately? (Owner: Marcus)
- Should the synthetic prompt set be reviewed by QA for potential blind spots? (Owner: Lena)

Document history: created 2025-11-12 by Aisha Raman; iterative updates during canary testing and postmortem 2026-02-28.

End of sheet.
